subject: Deployment mode follow-up & initial pricing (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up & initial pricing (Acme Health)

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups from our discovery so we can model options for you: 

Call recap:
- Primary goal: productionize real-time document ingestion + question-answering for clinical workflows.
- Throughput: expected steady-state ~10M tokens/month, with spikes up to ~150 QPS for short bursts.
- Latency target: sub-200ms P95 for user-facing queries.
- Compliance: must be HIPAA-ready; data residency in US required.
- Preference: you said a default preference for Private (VPC / on-prem), but open to Dedicated if the economics and SLAs align.

Immediate asks to help our cost model:
1) Confirm monthly token estimate (you mentioned ~10M tokens/month). Is that for input+output combined?
2) Typical prompt length (tokens) and average completion length?
3) Peak sustained QPS and expected burst duration.
4) Retention/LOB requirements for logging and audit trail (days).

Attached: a quick cost model template (acme_cost_model_v1.xlsx) and our deployment-mode one-pager (redwood_deployment_modes_onepager.pdf). I populated a few assumptions based on today’s call.

Short summary of options (high-level):
- Hosted API: lowest time-to-value; per-token pricing, no infra ops; not ideal if you need VPC or strict data isolation.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): dedicated GPU pools, predictable throughput and lower per-token equivalent if you commit; SLA-backed latency and data partitioning.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control and on-prem option for PHI, license + infra + support — higher upfront and predictable monthly platform fees; the unit economics depend on commit and infra choices.

Next steps: if you can confirm the items above, Marissa and I will build a side-by-side cost comparison (hosted per-token vs. dedicated reserved commits vs. private deployment TCO) and share by EOD Wednesday (Dec 2). Would you be available for a 30-minute follow-up Thursday to walk the model?

Thanks —
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_cost_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), redwood_deployment_modes_onepager.pdf (one-pager)

From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acmehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:40:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up & initial pricing (Acme Health)

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the recap and the docs — super helpful. Quick answers below: 

1) Token estimate: 10M tokens/month combined (input + output).
2) Typical prompt ~60 tokens, completion ~40 tokens on average.
3) Peak: we expect sustained spikes of ~150 QPS for 2–10 minute windows during batch runs; typical steady QPS ~8–12.
4) Retention: logs retained for 90 days; audit logs with access records required.

Regarding deployment preference: our security and compliance team prefers a Private VPC/on-prem option because of PHI handling, but procurement is highly sensitive to upfront costs. If Dedicated with a dedicated VPC and strict data separation gives materially better unit economics and an acceptable SOC2/HIPAA profile, we could consider that as well. Can you provide an example comparison with committed capacity sizes and what a 12‑month reserved commit looks like vs hosted per-token?

Also, please include any additional platform fees or support tiers we should expect for Private deployments (license, infra ops, monitoring).

I’m available for a follow-up on Thu, Dec 3 at 10:00am PT.

Best,
Alice Wong
Head of Data Platforms
Acme Health

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:05:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up & initial pricing (Acme Health)

Alice —

Appreciate the quick answers — that’s exactly what we need. High-level numbers below to set expectations; Marissa will run a detailed spreadsheet with your confirmed inputs and a 12-month committed scenario.

Hosted API (per-token):
- List price example: $0.0025 per 1K input tokens + $0.005 per 1K output tokens (example model).
- For 10M tokens/month (split 60/40 input/output) rough cost ~= $24–$30K/mo. No infra or platform fees beyond usage.

Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- Example reserved config: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved, optimized batching for throughput.
- Typical 12-month commit discount vs hosted can range 30–50% depending on commit and model footprint.
- Monthly platform fee and reserved capacity billing; unit economics improve if your sustained throughput is high and predictable.

Private (VPC / on-prem):
- Platform license + support + deployment services (one-time onboarding) + customer infra (HW + infra ops).
- Higher up-front/recurring base cost, but if you fully utilize the hardware and commit to multi-year contracts, TCO can be competitive versus hosted at high scale.

Attachments: initial_pricing_summary.pdf (high-level comparatives).

Next steps: Marissa — can you take Alice’s inputs and produce a side-by-side model for Thu (Dec 3) meeting? I’ll include a row-level comparison: hosted per-token, dedicated 12‑month commit (3 commit sizes), and private TCO (OPEX + amortized CapEx). Also include HIPAA/SOC2 notes and the security checklist.

Alice — we’ll send the spreadsheet and a calendar invite for Thu 10:00am PT.

Thanks,
Aditya
